issues: Scrambled numbering structure in the 'In View of:' list: items 11, 12, and 13 are merged into one line instead of being separate numbered items, which can break downstream boundary-based retrieval.
Meaning drift: "Dengan Persetujuan Bersama" was translated as "With Mutual Approval"; in this legal context it should be rendered as "With the Joint Approval" (of the DPRD and the Regent).
Scrambled/merged list structure: in Article 1 items 2–3 and 8–9 are run together on one line, breaking the numbered list boundaries.
Scrambled/merged list structure: in Article 3 lettered items a–f are merged (e.g., 'to: a.' inline; 'children:d.' and 'd... e...' on same line), breaking the lettered list boundaries.

Scrambled/merged list structure: in Article 4(4) lettered items a–e are merged with the lead-in text and with each other (e.g., 'related to:a.' and 'activities; e.'), breaking the lettered list boundaries.
Meaning drift/garbling in Article 1(17): 'and Indirect' is an incorrect/incomplete rendering of 'dan Tidak Langgsung' (should express both direct and indirect efforts).
Meaning drift in Article 2 letter c: "Pengayoman" translated as "Shelter"; more accurate is "Protection"/"Safeguarding".

Meaning drift in Article 1 item 17: Indonesian text ends with "dan Tidak Langgsung" (indirect) but translation renders it as "and indirect efforts" without reflecting the phrasing; should explicitly state both direct and indirect efforts.

Minor meaning/term accuracy: Article 1 item 11 "penjeratan uang" is closer to "debt bondage" (already present) but the clause structure should reflect that it is one of the means used; current wording is acceptable but can be tightened to mirror the original list structure.

Scrambled/merged list markers in multiple places (e.g., 'ande.', 'andg.', 'danc.', 'andh.', 'servicesd.', 'Economyc.', '(4)' merged into paragraph (3)); list item markers must appear once each and in the same order as the original.
Broken numbering structure: Article 8 paragraph (4) is merged into paragraph (3) instead of being a separate '(4)' item.
Minor meaning drift/terminology: 'ketenteraman dan ketertiban' rendered as 'peace and order' (better 'tranquility and public order'); keep legal sense consistent.
Scrambled/altered list structure in Article 8(3)-(4): original has item 3 followed immediately by item (4) on the same line; translation split them into separate lines and changed marker formatting.

Scrambled/altered list structure in Article 13(1): original has "c. Pelayanan hukumd. Pemulangan;" (missing separator) which requires preserving two separate items c and d; translation separated them but also changed punctuation/line-break structure (missing semicolon after c) and indentation differs from original marker style.

Scrambled/altered list structure in Article 13(2): original has "b. Ekonomic. Kesehatan;" (missing separator) which requires preserving two separate items b and c; translation separated them but removed the semicolon after b and changed marker formatting/indentation.

Meaning drift: Article 6(d) original contains a typo "dane."; translation silently corrected it. For downstream boundary matching, the marker sequence should reflect the original (d. then e.) but the text should not introduce/omit items—needs careful reconstruction while keeping intended items distinct.
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 19: item (1) and (2) sub-items a–e are run together (e.g., "with:a.", "ande.") instead of being separated as distinct list items.
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 20(2): sub-item d is merged into the preceding text ("andd.").
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 21: paragraph (2) is embedded in paragraph (1) and sub-items a–e are merged ("ande.") instead of being properly separated.
Scrambled/merged list structure in Article 23: sub-item c is merged ("andc.").

Scrambled list/numbering structure: in Article 19(1), Article 19(2), and Article 20(2) the original uses inline list markers (a., b., c., d., e.) on the same line as the preceding clause; the translation reformats them as indented sublists, changing the list-marker structure used for downstream splitting.
